result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password or Bitwarden**\. Both are excellent, but they serve slightly different priorities.

My overall recommendation is **1Password if ease of use matters most, and Bitwarden if value for money matters most.**

## My top 4 picks

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password Business**

(Best overall experience)

- Very intuitive for non-technical employees.
- Shared vaults with granular permissions.
- Admin controls, reporting and employee onboarding/offboarding.
- Excellent browser and mobile apps.

**Price\:** Around US\$8.99/user/month for Business, or a Teams Starter Pack for up to 10 users at US\$24.95/month, billed annually.

[1Password Business](https://1password.com/business)

---

![The best password managers in 2026 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/NzVuMgIchg5mHs-Kr9143cu9YVcLD78U-cfqnnpzpdksR6kB5LPVR6OyqUe0J0PAWilFgVX5RafeZ-AzNa_G6WUPgI8J1U4oAahEfqnQQL2SaxhVwFg9jy1o1kVewXMyq40iQ1cCkpkzpsh_DQntfgs6e3PLRpQFbO3dRcV-HQGbTSkVwYxuDvCJM657Aw6_?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden Teams**

(Best value)

- Open-source software.
- Secure shared collections.
- Admin console and audit logs.
- Good cross-platform support.
- Excellent value for growing teams.

**Price\:** US\$4/user/month, billed annually.

[Bitwarden Business](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

(Best for administration)

- Strong administrative controls.
- Shared folders and team permissions.
- Security reporting and auditing.
- Additional security features available.

**Price\:** Business plans start around US\$2/user/month for the limited Starter tier.

[Keeper Business](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

---

![The best password managers in 2025 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/S30I88layvxbkaDwXaWP5XnJ7U511ARCXJEcDjYd8i8QoMbXMBiKKYXroCriJ7kBR0oi7lM-NLlyOXMHqaLP4YKGj6rWlLsTvfSS4pKj24h_up7wZjWKu6xYF8rT-_7bc8XbvU4PlaIDiwcj88cnT8GVhbZrDMRuBptQttvTl2oiFqpoAxV9-pe3un--FrSZ?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Proton Pass**

- Privacy-focused approach.
- Secure credential sharing.
- Useful email alias functionality.
- Good choice for privacy-conscious teams.

**Price\:** Business plans start around US\$1.99/user/month, depending on tier.

[Proton Pass for Business](https://proton.me/business/pass)

Pricing is indicative, based on published 2026 pricing, generally with annual billing. Confirm Canadian pricing and taxes before purchasing. [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.northvetted.ca](https://www.northvetted.ca/reviews/best-password-manager-canada?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[vettlo.com](https://vettlo.com/tools/best-password-managers-for-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## Quick comparison

| Feature | 1Password | Bitwarden |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Ease of use | Excellent | Very good |
| Shared passwords | Yes | Yes |
| Employee permissions | Excellent | Good |
| Admin controls | Excellent | Very good |
| Open source | No | Yes |
| Value | Good | Excellent |


## What I'd prioritize for a small business

Regardless of which product you choose, make sure it supports\:

1. **Shared company vaults\:** Everyone can access the credentials they need without sharing passwords through email or Slack.
2. **Individual accounts\:** Never have employees share one master account.
3. **Two-factor authentication\:** Protect the password manager itself.
4. **Access revocation\:** Immediately remove access when an employee leaves.
5. **Granular permissions\:** Finance, management, IT and general employees should have different access.
6. **Emergency recovery\:** Have a secure process for recovering access if an administrator leaves.

## A couple of questions to narrow it down

I can give you a more precise recommendation if I know two things\:

**1\. How many people are on your team?**
